newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: KPN set for outright control of TNT after BT sells.
newsitem.headline: KPN set for outright control of TNT after BT sells.

text.p: Dutch postal and telecoms firm Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) on Friday said it had won majority control of transport giant TNT Ltd after Bankers Trust sold its blocking stake for a tidy profit.
Confident that its A$2 billion (US$1.62 billion) takeover was sure to succeed, KPN freed the friendly bid from all conditions and said the closing date had been extended to December 12.

KPN said in a statement issued after the share market closed that it held 51.9 percent of the express freight and logistics company following the purchase of 105 million shares from the local offshoot of the New York-based investment bank.
BT's stake of 19.9 percent had proved a temporary thorn in the side of KPN, which had placed a 90 percent acceptance condition on the bid for its European express freight partner.

While BT had intimated that it believed the A$2.45 per share offer was on the low side, other fund managers said its reluctance to bail out of the share register was nothing more than an arbitrage play.

Analysts said there was never much chance that KPN's bid would be matched by another express freight firm such as the once-touted Federal Express Corp because the offer price of A$2.45 per share was exceedingly generous for a company which had struggled financially in recent years.
The head of investment at a leading institution said he now expected other fund managers to quickly accept the KPN offer.
Australia's largest investor, the AMP Society, and UK-based funds manager Phillips & Drew Funds Management remain on the register with stakes of more than five percent.
An adviser to KPN, who asked not to be identified, said KPN hoped to quickly gain outright control of TNT and begin the promised strategic review of assets as soon as possible.
"We are confident that now KPN has control that shareholders will see the value of the offer and accept," the adviser said.
TNT shares traded at A$1.63 the day before the bid was announced at a joint news conference on October 2.
The bid has received regulatory approval from officials in Australia, Europe and the United States.
Analysts expect KPN to consider the sale of TNT's Asian operations as well as its half share in the AWAS aircraft leasing operation.
BT held about 16 percent of TNT before the bid was launched and paid between A$2.38 and A$2.43 per share for another 18 million shares after the bid was announced.
